among his best known compositions are orchestral works including enigma variations pomp and circumstance marches concertos for violin and cello and two symphonies he also composed choral works his roman catholicism was regarded with suspicion in some quarters and in class conscious society of victorian and edwardian britain he was acutely sensitive about his humble origins even after he achieved recognition he nevertheless married daughter of senior british army officer she inspired him both musically and socially but he struggled to achieve success until his forties when after series of moderately successful works his enigma variations 1899 became immediately popular in britain and overseas he followed variations with choral work dream of gerontius 1900 based on roman catholic text that caused some disquiet in anglican establishment in britain but it became and has remained core repertory work in britain and elsewhere his later full length religious choral works were well received but have not entered regular repertory in his fifties elgar composed symphony and violin concerto that were immensely successful his second symphony and his cello concerto did not gain immediate public popularity and took many years to achieve regular place in concert repertory of british orchestras elgar s music came in his later years to be seen as appealing chiefly to british audiences his stock remained low for generation after his death it began to revive significantly in 1960s helped by new recordings of his works some of his works have in recent years been taken up again internationally but music continues to be played more in britain than elsewhere elgar has been described as first composer to take gramophone seriously between 1914 and 1925 he w234424: northwestern knitting company factory building northwestern knitting company factory also known as munsingwear corporation and later as international market square is former factory building in sumner glenwood neighborhood of minneapolis minnesota united states company was founded in 1888 by george d munsing who invented method of plating wool fibers with silk and cotton to make union suit more comfortable company received financial backing from clinton morrison and charles alfred pillsbury who were prominent businessmen in minneapolis flour milling industry this style of underwear patented in 1891 proved to be very popular and company eventually became world s largest manufacturer of underwear company changed its name in 1919 to munsingwear company built five brick and concrete buildings between 1904 and 1915 eventually creating complex covering and employing up to 2000 workers five to eight story buildings had long rows of windows and although buildings mostly had plain appearance architects added some details such as slightly projecting cornices fretwork friezes and fluted doric columns oldest of buildings along glenwood avenue is notable for being city s first entirely reinforced concrete building engineer c p turner used concrete columns shaped like mushroom on top and he eventually patented this process which was widely used factory eventually closed in 1981 when economy reduced demand for munsingwear s products in 1985 buildings were renovated and complex was renamed international market square which housed offices shops and over 100 showrooms for home and office products renovation included five story atrium created by roofing over old courtyard where rail tracks once served complex in 2005 some portions of building were renovated into 96 loft apartments this was leading example of adaptive reuse in minneapolis building was listed on national register of historic places in 1983

w249219: quasi monte carlo method in numerical analysis quasi monte carlo method is method for numerical integration and solving some other problems using low discrepancy sequences also called quasi random sequences or sub random sequences this is in contrast to regular monte carlo method or monte carlo integration which are based on sequences of pseudorandom numbers monte carlo and quasi monte carlo methods are stated in similar way problem is to approximate integral of function f as average of function evaluated at set of points xx since we are integrating over s dimensional unit cube each x is vector of s elements difference between quasi monte carlo and monte carlo is way x are chosen quasi monte carlo uses low discrepancy sequence such as halton sequence sobol sequence or faure sequence whereas monte carlo uses pseudorandom sequence advantage of using low discrepancy sequences is faster rate of convergence quasi monte carlo has rate of convergence close to o 1 n whereas rate for monte carlo method is o n quasi monte carlo method recently became popular in area of mathematical finance or computational finance in these areas high dimensional numerical integrals where integral should be evaluated within threshold ε occur frequently hence monte carlo method and quasi monte carlo method are beneficial in these situations

w266484: east is east 1916 film east is east is 1916 british silent film drama directed by henry edwards who also starred in film with florence turner film is early example of plot premise which would prove very popular in british silent film canon that of character almost always pretty young girl from working class east end of london being suddenly thrust by circumstance into daunting milieu of west end high society full print of east is east survives and is well regarded by historians of british silent film writing for british film institute bryony dixon notes edwards seems to have had innate or instinctive understanding of cinema space both as actor and director and despite being hampered as everyone else at that early date by rather fixed sets and camera positions he uses himself and other actors to convey space beyond fourth wall creating illusion of satisfyingly convincing world she also notes locations are well chosen and evocative of bygone era particularly lovely scenes in kentish hop fields and that edith evans in very early screen role outrageously upstages everyone at every opportunity although largely serious drama film also includes scenes of visual humour arising from awkward collision of east end and west end manners and habits

w2103830: boise creek boise creek is stream in humboldt county california united states from its origin on orleans mountain it flows 8 5 miles to join klamath river about 2 25 miles southeast of orleans california creek lies within six rivers national forest and is part of lower klamath river watershed coho salmon oncorhynchus kisutch populations have declined dramatically in klamath river watershed due to eutrophication raised water temperatures and decreased stream flows induced by construction of dams especially in years of drought in addition dams have blocked access for salmon spawning grounds on over 300 miles of klamath river watershed coho salmon in southern oregon northern california coast soncc evolutionarily significant unit esu are federally listed as threatened and are also listed as threatened by california department of fish and game since 2002 access to boise creek for salmon has been blocked by bedrock falls 13 5 feet high near creekmouth see figure so mid klamath watershed council proposed in february 2010 creation of engineered logjam to divert flows into historic side channels which would re connect creek to klamath river mainstem and bypass falls before logjam could be constructed beaver coincidentally constructed dam across boise creek at proposed site and numerous coho salmon chinook salmon oncorhynchus tshawytscha and steelhead trout oncorhyncus mykiss are now accessing stream from klamath opening several new miles of historic spawning habitat to fish beaver dam has also created off channel ponds which have been shown to benefit coho by providing refuge from high flow conditions in main river and productive summer rearing habitat leading to as much as five fold increase in coho abundance as well as increased size it has also been shown that off channel wetlands enhance chinook salmon growth and survival

w2113983: john ii komnenos john ii komnenos or comnenus iōannēs ii komnēnos 13 september 1087 8 april 1143 was byzantine emperor from 1118 to 1143 also known as john beautiful or john goodkaloïōannēs he was eldest son of emperor alexios i komnenos and irene doukaina and second emperor to rule during komnenian restoration of byzantine empire john was pious and dedicated monarch who was determined to undo damage his empire had suffered following battle of manzikert half century earlier john has been assessed as greatest of komnenian emperors in course of his twenty five year reign john made alliances with holy roman empire in west decisively defeated pechenegs hungarians and serbs in balkans and personally led numerous campaigns against turks in asia minor john s campaigns fundamentally changed balance of power in east forcing turks onto defensive and restoring to byzantines many towns fortresses and cities right across anatolian peninsula in southeast john extended byzantine control from maeander in west all way to cilicia and tarsus in east in effort to demonstrate byzantine ideal of emperor s role as leader of christian world john marched into muslim syria at head of combined forces of byzantium and crusader states yet despite great vigour with which he pressed campaign john s hopes were disappointed by evasiveness of his crusader allies and their reluctance to fight alongside his forces under john empire s population recovered to about 10 million people quarter century of john ii s reign is less well recorded by contemporary or near contemporary writers than reigns of either his father alexios i or his son manuel i in particular little is known of history of john s domestic rule or policies

w2134311: midnight ramble film midnight ramble is 1994 documentary about early history of black american movies from period between 1910 and 1950 known as race movies these films traditionally independent of hollywood were made primarily by for and about black community this documentary is tribute to film genre that lasted for more than 40 years produced over 500 movies and created foundation for contemporary films from directors such as spike lee and tyler perry james avery narrates this exploration of early black film industry there is mistaken assumption that race films began largely in reaction to d w griffith s 1915 birth of nation nothing could be further from truth race movies actually began around 1910 in chicago in response to black community longing to see themselves reflected on silver screen via this new medium of film wanting to see themselves through their own eyes on their own terms thus counteracting hollywood stereotypes within american media film focuses especially on work of oscar micheaux considered dean of black american film controversial filmmaker who wrote produced and directed over 40 features and tackled difficult social issues in black america it includes clips from films by number of african american directors of period which is very helpful since many of these films are difficult to find or unavailable there are two versions of title of documentary both referring to same work initially released in 1994 as midnight ramble oscar micheaux story of race movies it was re released as midnight ramble story of black film industry by pbs in 1995 1995 version also eliminates david mccullugh introduction

w2139909: pall mall magazine pall mall magazine was monthly british literary magazine published between 1893 and 1914 begun by william waldorf astor as offshoot of pall mall gazette magazine included poetry short stories serialized fiction and general commentaries along with extensive artwork it was notable in its time as first british magazine to publish illustrations in number and finish comparable to those of american periodicals of same class much of which was in late pre raphaelite style it was often compared to competing publication strand magazine many artists such as illustrator sidney paget and author h g wells sold freelance work to both during its run magazine published many of most significant artists of day including illustrators george morrow and edmund joseph sullivan poets algernon charles swinburne and rudyard kipling and authors such as julian osgood field bernard capes charlotte o conor eccles jack london and joseph conrad whose novel typhoon was first serialized therein among magazine s editors were douglas straight 1893 1896 lord frederick spencer hamilton 1896 1900 george halkett 1901 1905 and charles morley 1905 1914 on october 6 1912 new york times reported that waldorf astor had sold magazine said to have obtained very little for it in 1914 as romantic ideas faded with onset of first world war pall mall magazine merged with nash s magazine controlled by hearst corporation since 1910 to become nash s pall mall magazine from may 1927 two magazines were again published separately but they were re merged after september 1929 issue and finally ceased publication altogether following issue of september 1937

w2143360: charlie chaplin sir charles spencer chaplin 16 april 1889 25 december 1977 was english comic actor filmmaker and composer who rose to fame in era of silent film he became worldwide icon through his screen persona tramp and is considered one of most important figures in history of film industry his career spanned more than 75 years from childhood in victorian era until year before his death in 1977 and encompassed both adulation and controversy chaplin s childhood in london was one of poverty and hardship as his father was absent and his mother struggled financially and he was sent to workhouse twice before age of nine when he was 14 his mother was committed to mental asylum chaplin began performing at early age touring music halls and later working as stage actor and comedian at 19 he was signed to prestigious fred karno company which took him to america he was scouted for film industry and began appearing in 1914 for keystone studios he soon developed tramp persona and formed large fan base he directed his own films and continued to hone his craft as he moved to essanay mutual and first national corporations by 1918 he was one of best known figures in world in 1919 chaplin co founded distribution company united artists which gave him complete control over his films his first feature length film was kid 1921 followed by woman of paris 1923 gold rush 1925 and circus 1928 he refused to move to sound films in 1930s instead producing city lights 1931 and modern times 1936 without dialogue he became increasingly political and his next film great dictator 1940 satirized adolf hitler 1940s were decade marked with controversy for chaplin and his popularity declined rapidly he was accused of communist sympathies while he created scandal through his involvement in paternity suit and his marriages to much younger women fbi investigation was opened and chaplin was forced to leave united states and settle in switzerland he abandoned tramp in his later films which include monsieur verdoux 1947 limelight 1952 king in new york 1957 and countess from hong kong 1967 chaplin wrote directed produced edited starred in and composed music for most of his films he was perfectionist and his financial independence enabled him to spend years on development and production of picture his films are characterized by slapstick combined with pathos typified in tramp s struggles against adversity many contain social and political themes as well as autobiographical elements he received honorary academy award for incalculable effect he has had in making motion pictures art form of this century in 1972 as part of renewed appreciation for his work he continues to be held in high regard with gold rushcity lightsmodern times and great dictator often ranked on lists of greatest films of all time

w2190084: adam mickiewicz adam bernard mickiewicz 24 december 179826 november 1855 was polish poet dramatist essayist publicist translator professor of slavic literature and political activist he is regarded as national poet in poland lithuania and belarus principal figure in polish romanticism he is counted as one of poland s three bards trzej wieszcze and is widely regarded as poland s greatest poet he is also considered one of greatest slavic and european poets and has been dubbed slavic bard leading romantic dramatist he has been compared in poland and europe to byron and goethe he is known chiefly for poetic drama dziadyforefathers eve and national epic poem pan tadeusz his other influential works include konrad wallenrod and grażyna all these served as inspiration for uprisings against three imperial powers that had partitioned polish lithuanian commonwealth out of existence mickiewicz was born in russian partitioned territories of former grand duchy of lithuania which had been part of polish lithuanian commonwealth and was active in struggle to win independence for his home region after as consequence spending five years exiled to central russia in 1829 he succeeded in leaving russian empire and like many of his compatriots lived out rest of his life abroad he settled first in rome then in paris where for little over three years he lectured on slavic literature at collège de france he died probably of cholera at constantinople in ottoman empire where he had gone to help organize polish and jewish forces to fight russia in crimean war in 1890 his remains were repatriated from montmorency val d oise in france to wawel cathedral in kraków poland

w2196403: i am lonesome hobo i am lonesome hobo is song written and recorded by bob dylan released in 1967 on his eighth studio album john wesley harding lyrics to i am lonesome hobo tells of typical riches to rags tradition where man openly admits to being hobo having tried my hand at bribery blackmail and deceit yet has served time for ev rything cept beggin on street dylan s style of writing often leans towards writing ballads that present his listeners with chance to get inside minds of social outcasts perspective that everyday people may overlook or misunderstand this hobo has seen it all once being affluent yet selfish man unable to trust anybody including his own brother hobo s isolation began not with his loss of wealth but with effect that wealth had upon him in first place as song reaches its final verse hobo offers advice to common people as he plans to continue his misinterpreted wandering asking them to stay free from petty jealousies live by no man s code and hold your judgment for yourself lest you wind up on this road within his solitariness hobo has found certain philosophical stability leaving him standing in garb of prophet rather than beggar this hobo s warning before his departure holds true to writing style dylan approaches with ending of many of his songs offering lyrically and vocally driven picture of life that is not typically lived or even considered haunting harmonica assertive drum beat and acoustic guitar incorporates well with clearly pronounced and elongated wordplay song features some of dylan s most controlled singing most likely being rhetorical decision on dylan s part because hobos are typically known for being wanderers lacking any insight or socially acceptable manners dylan however seems to put this character on level socially where one would not typically place vagabond providing idea that hobo can be wise man rather than some socially awkward bum

w2196551: edward latham ormerod edward latham ormerod frs md 27 august 1819 18 march 1873 was english physician and amateur entomologist he was born in london seventh of ten children of george ormerod cheshire historian and his wife sarah latham eldest daughter of physician john latham his younger sister was eleanor anne ormerod he was educated at rugby school until 1838 was student at st bartholomew s hospital london until october 1841 and then went up to gonville and caius college cambridge there he was awarded classical scholarship and afterwards scholarships in anatomy and chemistry and graduated m b in 1846 and m d in 1851 he returned to st bartholomew s in 1846 to work in post mortem room as demonstrator until health problems obliged him to move to brighton in 1847 to practise as physician he was elected fellow of royal college of physicians and in 1851 delivered their gulstonian lectures on subject of valvular disease of heart in 1853 he was appointed physician to sussex county hospital during this time he published number of papers on medicine and natural history his publication of british social wasps in 1868 secured his election as fellow of royal society on 6 june 1872 he died in 1873 of disease of bladder he had married in 1853 mary olivia porter who died later same year and in 1856 maria millett with whom he had six children one of his sons was physician sir arthur latham ormerod oxford s first medical officer for health
w2196552: edward ormerod edward ormerod 2 may 1834 26 may 1894 was english mining engineer edward ormerod sometimes ormrod was born on 2 may 1834 in village of church near accrington in lancashire england he worked as mining engineer at fletcher burrows and company s gibfield colliery in atherton greater manchester where he devised and tested safety device he was supported by chief engineering foreman james rothwell from hindley he married betsy hope in 1856 and had several children he died on 26 may 1894 and is buried in atherton cemetery small memorial stone in front of his grave depicts and pays tribute to his invention edward ormerod developed and patented ormerod safety link or detaching hook known in mining circles as butterfly this elegant device was inserted into winding rope in such way that if lift cage was accidentally overwound link would be pulled into bell through which winding rope passed this action would not only disconnect cage from winding rope but also prevent cage from falling back down shaft device was patented in 1867 and is manufactured today it is believed that lives of many miners have been saved by its use and it has never failed in service design was awarded gold medal at manchester mechanical industrial exhibition of 1875 and silver medal at franco british exhibition in 1908

w2206127: evelyn nesbit evelyn nesbit born florence evelyn nesbit december 25 1884 or 1885 january 17 1967 was american artists model chorus girl and actress in early part of 20th century nesbit s figure and face appeared frequently in mass circulation newspapers and magazine advertisements on souvenir items and in calendars making her celebrity her career began in her early teens in philadelphia and continued in new york where she posed for cadre of respected artists of era including james carroll beckwith frederick s church and notably charles dana gibson who idealized her as gibson girl she had distinction of being early fashion and artists model in era when both fashion photography as advertising medium and pin up as art genre were just beginning their ascendancy nesbit received further worldwide attention when her husband mentally unstable multimillionaire harry kendall thaw shot and killed prominent architect and new york socialite stanford white in front of hundreds of witnesses at rooftop theatre of madison square garden on evening of june 25 1906 leading to what press would call trial of century during trial nesbit testified that five years earlier when she was stage performer at age of 15 or 16 she had attracted attention of white who first gained her and her mother s trust then sexually assaulted her while she was unconscious and then had subsequent romantic and sexual relationship with her that continued for some time

w2222287: prom night 1980 film prom night is 1980 canadian slasher film directed by paul lynch written by william gray and starring jamie lee curtis and leslie nielsen plot follows group of high school seniors who are targeted at their prom by masked killer seeking vengeance for accidental death of young girl six years earlier it features supporting performances from casey stevens eddie benton mary beth rubens and michael tough prom night was filmed in toronto in late 1979 on budget of 1 5 million distributed by avco embassy pictures it premiered in united states in july 1980 in select cities and was immediate financial success its release platform expanded to major cities such as los angeles and new york in august where it was again met with high box office receipts at time film was avco embassy s most financially successful release breaking weekend records in los angeles philadelphia and new england by end of its theatrical run prom night had grossed 15 million in united states and was canada s highest earning horror film of 1980 critical reaction to film varied with some such as roger ebert and gene siskel dismissing it for its depictions of violence against women while others alternately praised film for its more muted violent content prom night received some critical accolades garnering genie award nominations for editing and for curtis s leading performance alternative cut of film was popularly aired on american and canadian television networks in 1981 in intervening years prom night has accrued substantial cult following not only for its horror content but also for its disco heavy soundtrack which was released by rca records in japan in 1980 some film scholars have cited prom night as one of most influential slasher films of period several companies released film on video and it was distributed on dvd by anchor bay entertainment in 1998 remastered blu ray edition was released by synapse films in 2014

w2308550: alan fox sociologist alan fox dfm 23 january 1920 26 june 2002 was english industrial sociologist who revolutionised separate discipline of industrial relations fox who grew up in manor park joined royal air force raf and applied for aircrew training but was rejected due to poor eyesight he served initially as ground staff photographer in india and burma with rank of corporal he independent institution in oxford fox then entered university of oxford where he spent majority of his academic career studying economics and political science at exeter college in 1950 while lecturing at ruskin he completed bachelor of letters b litt thesis on history of industrial relations in black country that same year fox married margaret dow with whom he had two sons in 1958 he industrial relations written for donovan royal commission on trade unions and employers associations 1965 68 in it he described dominance in industrial relations of two rival ideological theoretical perspectives first for which fox coined name unitary later unitarist denies that interests of employers and employees were significantly different from each other for other perspective he used existing term from political science pluralist perspective which suggests that multiple parties are involved in decision making however fox himself was strongly influenced by third major theoretical position radical perspective especially marxism with and hugh clegg fox became prominent in group of scholars known collectively as oxford school of industrial relations although oxford school was w2326627: ludwig von buhl ludwig von buhl 4 january 1816 30 july 1880 was german pathologist born in munich he studied medicine in munich and vienna and in 1847 was habilitated as lecturer of pathological anatomy and microscopy at university of munich in 1850 he was chosen as associate professor and from 1854 served as prosector at university general hospital in 1859 he was appointed professor of general pathology and pathological anatomy in munich where in 1875 he became director of pathological institute two of his better known assistants were ernst schweninger 1850 1924 and wilhelm heinrich erb 1840 1921 with max pettenkofer 1818 1901 carl von voit 1831 1908 and ludwig adolph timotheus radlkofer 1829 1927 he published biological journal zeitschrift für biologie his best written effort was 1872 lungenentzündung tuberkulose und schwindsucht book that was later translated into english as inflammation of lungs tuberculosis and consumption 1874 buhl is remembered for his work with infectious diseases in particular pioneer research of miliary tuberculosis with austrian pathologist franz dittrich 1815 1859 is obtained buhl dittrich law supposition that states that in every case of acute miliary tuberculosis there exists at least one old focus of causation in body his name is associated with buhl s disease rare disorder of newborns that he first described in 1861 disease is defined as acute parenchymatous fatty degeneration of liver kidney or heart combined with hemorrhages into various organs

w2326632: wilhelm von mirbach wilhelm maria theodor ernst richard graf von mirbach harff 2 july 1871 6 july 1918 was german diplomat born in bad ischl in upper austria into catholic rhenan aristocratic family he was scion of founder of knight academy his parents were ernst graf von mirbach and his wife wilhelmine von thun hohenstein 1851 1929 from 1908 to 1911 mirbach served as embassy clerk in saint petersburg and then as political councillor for german military command in bucharest in 1915 he became german ambassador in greece before being expelled from athens in december 1916 when entente leaning government of eleftherios venizelos took power he participated in russian german negotiations in brest litovsk from december 1917 to march 1918 he was appointed german ambassador to russia in april 1918 mirbach was assassinated at german embassy in moscow by yakov grigorevich blumkin and nikolai andreyev at request of central committee of left socialist revolutionaries who tried to incite war between russia and germany blumkin entered mirbach s residence in moscow using forged papers and shot his victim at point blank range as mirbach tried to escape andreyev fired second bullet and both of assassins leapt out of window and then drove away in cheka car mirbach s assassination signaled beginning of revolt of left socialist revolutionaries in moscow in 1918 mirbach was succeeded as german ambassador to russia by karl helfferich coincidentally later relative andreas von mirbach would be murdered by red army faction at west german embassy siege in stockholm in 1975

w2327959: tutankhamun s trumpets tutankhamun s trumpets are pair of trumpets found in burial chamber of 18th dynasty pharaoh tutankhamun trumpets one of sterling silver and one of bronze or copper are considered to be oldest operational trumpets in world and only known surviving examples from ancient egypt trumpets were found in 1922 by howard carter during excavation of tutankhamun s tomb bronze trumpet was discovered in tomb s antechamber in large chest containing various military objects and walking sticks silver trumpet was subsequently found in burial chamber both are finely engraved with decorative images of gods ra horakhty ptah and amun silver trumpet s bell is engraved with whorl of sepals and calices representing lotus flower and praenomen and nomen of king bronze trumpet may in fact be made of copper metal has not yet been analysed similar looking trumpets feature in egyptian wall paintings that are usually though not always associated with military scenes silent for over 3 000 years trumpets were sounded before live audience of estimated 150 million listeners through international bbc broadcast aired on 16 april 1939 trumpets were played by bandsman james tappern of prince albert s own 11th royal hussars regiment recording was recently featured and can be heard on bbc radio 4 program ghost music rex keating who presented 1939 broadcast later claimed that during rehearsal silver trumpet shattered and alfred lucas member of carter s team who had restored finds was so distressed he needed to go to hospital due to their fragility it is unlikely trumpets will be played again in any official musical reconstructions

w2371337: antiochus xi epiphanes antiochus xi epiphanes philadelphus unknown 93 bc was hellenistic seleucid monarch who reigned as king of syria between 94 and 93 bc he was son of antiochus viii and his wife tryphaena antiochus xi s early life was time of constant civil war between his father and his uncle antiochus ix conflict ended with assassination of antiochus viii followed by establishment of antiochus ix in antioch capital of syria antiochus viii s eldest son seleucus vi in control of western cilicia marched against his uncle and had him killed taking antioch for himself only to be expelled from it and driven to his death in 94 bc by antiochus ix s son antiochus x following murder of seleucus vi antiochus xi declared himself king jointly with his twin brother philip i dubious ancient accounts which may be contradicted by archaeological evidence report that antiochus xi s first act was to avenge his late brother by destroying mopsuestia in cilicia city responsible for death of seleucus vi in 93 bc antiochus xi took antioch event not mentioned by ancient historians but confirmed through numismatic evidence antiochus xi appears to have been senior king minting coinage as sole king and reigning alone in capital while philip i remained in cilicia but kept his royal title antiochus xi may have restored temple of apollo and artemis in daphne but his reign did not last long in autumn of same year antiochus x regrouped and counter attacked antiochus xi was defeated and drowned in orontes river as he tried to flee
w2371338: seleucus vi epiphanes seleucus vi epiphanes nicator between 124 and 109 bc 94bc was hellenistic seleucid monarch who ruled syria between 96 and 94 bc he was son of antiochus viii and his egyptian wife tryphaena seleucus vi lived in period of civil war between his father and his uncle antiochus ix which ended in 96 bc when antiochus viii was assassinated antiochus ix then occupied capital antioch while seleucus vi established his power base in western cilicia and himself prepared for war in 95 bc antiochus ix marched against his nephew but lost battle and was killed seleucus vi became master of capital but had to share syria with his brother demetrius iii based in damascus and his cousin antiochus ix s son antiochus x according to ancient historian appian seleucus vi was violent ruler he taxed his dominions extensively to support his wars and resisted allowing cities measure of autonomy as had been practice of former kings his reign did not last long in 94 bc he was expelled from antioch by antiochus x who followed him to cilician city of mopsuestia seleucus took shelter in city where his attempts to raise money led to riots that eventually claimed his life in 94 bc ancient traditions have different versions of his death but he was most probably burned alive by rioters following his demise his brothers antiochus xi and philip i destroyed mopsuestia as act of revenge and their armies fought those of antiochus x

w2372895: thrill book thrill book was u s pulp magazine published by street smith in 1919 it was intended to carry different stories this meant stories that were unusual or unclassifiable which in practice often meant that stories were fantasy or science fiction first eight issues edited by harold hersey were mixture of adventure and weird stories contributors included greye la spina charles fulton oursler j h coryell and seabury quinn hersey was replaced by ronald oliphant with july 1 issue probably because street smith were unhappy with his performance oliphant printed more science fiction and fantasy than hersey had done though this included two stories by murray leinster which hersey had purchased before being replaced most famous story from thrill book is heads of cerberus very early example of novel about alternate time tracks by francis stevens oliphant was given larger budget than hersey and was able to acquire material by popular writers such as h bedford jones but he was only able to produce eight more issues before end came last issue was dated october 15 1919 it was probably cancelled because of poor sales although printers strike at that time may have been factor although thrill book has been described as first american pulp to specialize in fantasy and science fiction this description is not supported by recent historians of field who regard it instead as stepping stone on path that ultimately led to weird tales and amazing stories first true specialized magazines in fields of weird fiction and science fiction respectively

of raf existed on paper from 1919 first person to hold rank was lord hugh trenchard from 1927 in uk rank has often been held by most senior actively serving raf officer whereas in other commonwealth he trained him in particular area of hadith scholarship and al haythami was to achieve distinction in this field and to produce highly valuable works in it this is area of zawa id which we will presently discuss al haythami was exemplary in his religious devotion and his serious approach to hadith scholarship he cared little for worldly matters which are main preoccupation of many people w2404169: phintys phintys was pythagorean philosopher probably from third century bc she wrote work on correct behaviour of women two extracts of which are preserved by stobaeus according to stobaeus phintys was daughter of callicrates who is otherwise unknown holger thesleff suggests that this callicrates might be identified with callicratidas spartan general who died at battle of arginusae if so this would make phintys spartan and date her birth to late fifth century bc and her floruit to fourth century i m plant considers this emendation fanciful iamblichus mentions philtys in his list of female pythagoreans he says that she was from croton and that her father was called theophrius i m plant believes that iamblichus philtys though also pythagorean and similarly named is distinct from stobaeus phintys two fragments attributed to phintys are preserved in stobaeus however not all scholars agree that fragments are authentic lefkowitz and fant argue that works attributed to female pythagoreans including phintys were actually rhetorical exercises written by men they are written in doric dialect and amount to about 80 lines of prose language used dates to around fourth century bc although some features of it appear to be deliberate archaisms it was likely actually composed in third century bc though date as late as second century ad was suggested by friedrich wilhelm in 1915 fragments discuss differences between men and women and argues for chastity as most important virtue for women she gives series of ways that women ought to practice self control concluding that most effective way is to only have sex with her husband in order to produce legitimate children along with her defence of women s chastity phintys argues that practice of philosophy is appropriate for women as well as men
